The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. 
The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Contractors for the ECLS MPEV Valves for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
 The Manual Pressure Equalization Valve is part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module. 
The Manual Pressure Equalization Valve (MPEV) is used to equalize pressure across adjacent volumes (e.g. vestibules, modules), releasing atmosphere from the module with higher pressure towards the one with lower pressure. The valve can be operated manually on both sides, requiring no electrical interface.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon
